text:
A: Hello! Hi, can you hear me okay? Sorry, my screen froze for a second there.
B: Hiya, yeah, I can hear you fine. I'm Hannah. I'm in Norwich.
A: Lovely. I'm Nadeesha, I'm in Cardiff. Sorry, I'm always a bit nervous with these video things, you know, in case something goes wrong.
B: Oh, same. I was convinced my laptop was going to die during that puzzle bit. Did you finish it?
A: Erm, mostly? I got stuck on the last one, actually. I kept thinking there was a trick. How about you?
B: No, I ran out of time. I'm rubbish at that sort of thing under pressure. Give me an essay and I'm fine.
A: An essay? Are you studying?
B: Yeah, part-time with the Open University, Arts and Humanities. I'm in my third year. I do it in the evenings once my daughter's in bed, so it's a lot of late nights and cups of tea. In the day I'm a senior midday supervisor at a primary school, so lunchtimes, the playground, all the fallouts. And I do breakfast club as well, which is honestly my favourite bit.
A: Oh, that's lovely. That's a lot, actually, with a little one. How old is she?
B: Isla's nine. She's obsessed with drawing horses at the moment, just horses, on everything.
A: Aw. My daughter is eight, Sanuli. With her it's swimming. Tuesdays are swimming lessons, so Tuesdays are a nightmare for me, sorry, not a nightmare, just very rushed.
B: No, nightmare's fair, I get it. What do you do, then?
A: I'm a senior procurement officer for one of the health boards here, so NHS. Basically I manage the tenders and the supplier contracts for medical consumables, gloves, dressings, syringes, that sort of thing. It sounds boring, but actually it's quite a lot of negotiating, and I like that part. I like being the one in the meeting who has actually read the contract, you know?
B: Ha, that's a good skill. I bet the suppliers hate you.
A: Some of them, maybe! This week was all supplier meetings, so I'm knackered, honestly. Is that the right word, knackered?
B: That's exactly the right word. I'm knackered most Fridays. Chips Friday at school is chaos, the queue goes round the hall.
A: I can imagine. And what do you want to do with the degree? Sorry, is that too nosy?
B: No, not at all. I'd love to go into museum learning, like running school workshops at Norwich Castle or somewhere like that. I volunteered at a half-term family day and absolutely loved it. It's taken me a while to get here, I left uni at nineteen because I was skint, so this is sort of round two.
A: That's really nice, actually. I think it's good to do it when you really want it, no?
B: Yeah, I hope so. Fingers crossed. Do you get to travel much, with work and Sanuli?
A: Erm, we go back to Sri Lanka every other year, for a month. My family is in Kandy. And we try to do a city break. Last year was Lisbon, which was beautiful. We stayed in a really nice hotel near the river.
B: Oh, I'd love Lisbon. My dream is Florence, to see the actual frescoes. I've got a little savings jar for it. Very slowly.
A: You should go! Florence is meant to be amazing. Erm, sorry, I don't know much about frescoes, actually. Are they the paintings on the walls?
B: Yeah, painted straight onto wet plaster. My course has me looking at medieval wall paintings, so I've gone a bit nerdy about it.
A: No, that's interesting. Sanuli would like that, she loves painting. Is that okay, sorry, I keep talking about my daughter.
B: Don't be daft, I've been going on about horses! Does she draw as well, or is it more...
